result.title: Timer-M1: A Multivariate Time Series Foundation Model via Learning Primitives
result.summary: We introduce Timer-M1, a pretrained multivariate time series foundation model that learns with primitives for zero-shot forecasting. Across domains, time series share elementary temporal and relational patterns, termed primitives, yet differ in how these primitives manifest and evolve across different contexts. Despite progress in zero-shot and task-general forecasting, existing foundation models may still struggle to generalize to complex real-world scenarios. To this end, we develop a primitive-based data synthesis and pretraining pipeline. The synthesis pipeline generates series with temporal primitives shared across domains and then assembles real and generated series into multivariate samples using relational primitives. Afterwards, samples are organized into episodes by assigning distinct channel roles as target variates, past-only covariates, and known-future covariates, ensuring that the model is optimized on predictable variates using available exogenous information. Technically, Timer-M1 further adapts gated two-dimensional Transformer blocks that dynamically allocate cross-variate attention across layers. Across three large-scale forecasting benchmarks, Timer-M1 ranks first on both FEV and TIME and second on GIFT-Eval among most recent time series foundation models. These results support effective primitive-based pretraining as a route to robust general forecasting technique across domains and task settings.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Timer-M1，一个多变量时间序列基础模型：先用跨域共享的时序基元和关系基元合成数据并拼装多变量样本，再按不同通道角色组织成 episode 预训练，配合门控二维 Transformer 动态分配跨变量注意力，实现零样本预测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「基元 + 角色化 episode」的预训练思路可能与 LVR 的状态抽象、可复用推理基元及监督贡献分配存在概念关联，可供核查，但该文不涉及视觉或多模态推理，迁移线索较远。
